title: Rating Inputs Bulletin: Elevation Certificates on the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
Under Risk Rating 2.0 the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own) do not require an Elevation Certificate to rate the policy, and a first floor height certified on an Elevation Certificate replaces the rating engine's estimated first floor height.

| Tier | Elevation Certificate required for rating | Certified first floor height replaces the engine's estimate |
|---|---|---|
| NFIP General Property Form – Non-Residential Condominium Unit | no | yes |
| NFIP General Property Form – Non-Residential Manufactured Building | no | yes |
| NFIP General Property Form – Other Residential Building | no | yes |
| NFIP General Property Form – Non-Residential Building | no | yes |
| NFIP RCBAP – Two-to-Four Unit Condominium Building | no | yes |
| NFIP RCBAP – Five-or-More Unit Condominium Building | no | yes |

- **Not required.** On no tier is an Elevation Certificate a condition of rating the policy.
- **Used when supplied.** On every tier a certified first floor height is the one the rating engine uses in place of its own estimate.

## Parameter meanings

- Whether an Elevation Certificate is required to rate the policy under Risk Rating 2.0; boolean.
- Whether a first floor height certified on an Elevation Certificate replaces the rating engine's estimated first floor height; boolean.
